claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance.
A thin, uniform Al2O3 coating will significantly improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 coating will preserve the alloy's room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical properties.
A thin, uniform Al2O3 coating is to be deposited on the alloy surface, potentially by physical vapor deposition.
The proposed oxidation exposure is air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
The Al2O3 coating acts as a physical and chemical barrier to oxygen diffusion into the substrate.
Suppressing oxygen diffusion with the coating prevents detrimental internal oxidation and pesting.
The alumina layer forms a stable, slow-growing oxide scale.
The alumina scale adheres strongly to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The passivating alumina barrier limits oxygen ingress, mitigates pesting, and thereby maintains the alloy's mechanical properties.
Coated specimens will have lower oxidation mass gain than uncoated specimens after the specified exposure.
Coated specimens will exhibit less internal oxidation than uncoated specimens after the specified exposure.
Coated specimens will retain their ductility and high-temperature strength after exposure.
Uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant oxidation, pesting, and mechanical-property degradation in air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
Similar coating strategies have improved oxidation resistance in related non-equiatomic alloys.
Differences in substrate chemistry and coating adhesion may prevent the coating from performing optimally on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.

contradictions.description: The conditions refer to mechanical loading similar to standard tensile testing, whereas the boundary limits applicability to minimal mechanical loading. It is unclear whether tensile loading occurs during oxidation or only afterward.
